# T6.07: HEVC P-frames

`encodeN -hevc` (IDR + P, constant QP). Three fixes took the first P picture from an engine fault to a clean
60-frame stream; multiple references don't work yet, so HEVC uses one.

## Fixes

1. **`nvenc_h265_slice_control_s.slice_type` is numbered like `pic_type` (0 P, 1 B, 2 I)**, not as the header's
   comment says (0 B, 1 P, 2 I). With 1 the engine faulted on the first P picture (`info32 0x1f`); nullmoth's library
   sends 0 for its P slices (the slice header in the stream still says P).
2. **Reference addresses by position in list 0**: for HEVC the reference of list entry *i* goes to `SET_IN_REF_PIC<i>`
   (`poc_entry_l0[i] = i`), while `pic_control.l0[i]` keeps 2 x the DPB slot (nullmoth's third picture: `l0[0]` 2, the
   reference in `REF_PIC0`). H.264 used `REF_PIC<slot>`. With slot indexing the second P picture faulted.
3. As nullmoth's: `temp_dist_l0` -1 after the last reference, `diff_pic_order_cnt_zero[0]` = 0xfefefefe,
   `same_poc[0]` 1, `dist_scale_factor[0][0]` 256; inline short-term RPS (one picture back, used), and the slice
   overrides the active reference count.

The `l0` question from T6.03 is answered by fix 2.

## Results (one reference, `encodeN -hevc W H N QP_I QP_P 1`)

| stream | rate at 60 fps | luma (avg / min) | decode errors |
|---|---|---|---|
| 256x128, 60 frames, QP 22/25 | 0.22 Mbit/s | 49.70 / 49.11 dB | 0 |
| 1280x720, 60 frames, IDR every 20 | 4.17 Mbit/s | 50.20 / 49.47 dB | 0 |
| 1920x1080, 60 frames, QP 22/28 | 6.29 Mbit/s | 48.34 / 47.80 dB | 0 |
| 3840x2160, 60 frames, QP 22/25 | 30.15 Mbit/s | 50.21 / 49.54 dB | 0 |
| 3840x2160, 60 frames, QP 20/32 | 21.25 Mbit/s | 44.62 / 44.06 dB | 0 |

Same 4K content and QPs with our H.264: 52.39 Mbit/s at 48.71 dB. **HEVC: 42 % less rate, 1.5 dB better**, at the
same encode time (4.13 vs 3.95 ms per 4K frame).

## Open: two or more references

With 2 or 3 references the stream breaks at the first picture that has two (picture 2: 20.7 dB, then lower), though the
slice headers are right (RPS POC -1, -2, -3, all used; active count overridden). The engine predicts from reference
index 1 differently than the header says. Filling `dist_scale_factor` with HEVC's MV scaling factors (tb/td, stored
[source][target]) helps (13 -> 25 dB) but doesn't fix it; `same_poc` variants and `l0` = 2 x list position change
nothing. nullmoth's library only ever uses one active reference, so there is no working example to observe. For now
`enc_open` clamps HEVC to `num_refs` 1 (what VideoToolbox sessions use anyway).
